search_notes.notes:
I returned 9 candidates, fewer than the 18 asked for. Many results either had no Canton Fair evidence or were knit-led, so I left them out.

What worked best: Zhejiang government exhibitor and booth-allocation PDFs on zjjcmspublic.oss-cn-hangzhou-zwynet-d01-a.internet.cloud.zj.gov.cn. Shaoxing has lists for the 134th, 136th and 137th sessions, Huzhou for the 137th, Hangzhou for the 136th and Jiaxing (Pinghu) for the 137th. WebFetch could not read them, but pdftotext could. Keqiao Daily and China Textile News reports on the 136th and 139th fairs also helped. The Shaoxing government page for the 138th list (sx.gov.cn) returned 503.

Most names on the Shaoxing lists are small 进出口 or 贸易 (trading) companies, or knit mills, and most have no web footprint I could match.

Excluded:
- Knit-led: Shaoxing Sanzhi, Mianguan, Suerte, Zhejiang ESSE/Real Textile, Huzhou Tianyi (mainly warp knit), Qida, Fumeida, Qingsong (home textile and warp knit).
- Traders or converters: Harbour Textile & Garments (Trade Company with 5-50 staff; its 138th booth showed suits), Linen Origin (Trading Company), Fantasy/凡特思.
- Outside the slice's regions: Hebei and Guangzhou mills.

Shaoxing Newwuhuan Textiles fits the slice very well (TR suiting, thobe fabric, Middle East exports), but I found no Canton Fair evidence for it, so it is not included. Layer 2 could look for it separately.

I found no Lanxi exhibitors. I found no Shaoxing nida or thobe mills with Canton Fair evidence.

Pages I could not open: yilinfabric.com (HTTP 429), harboursx.com and chinacaidie.com (HTTP 503). I avoided growsmilingly.cn because its pages look like a mirror of Canton Fair data.

I found 16 candidates (the quota was 18). 11 have strong Canton Fair evidence and 5 have medium. Nine of the strong ones are in Shijiazhuang or Shengze.

What worked:
- Chinese news reports were the best source. Shijiazhuang reports on the 137th and 139th fairs (texnet.com.cn, ctn1986.com, sjz.gov.cn) and Shengze delegation reports on the 136th and 139th fairs (jstv.com, ctn1986.com) gave named exhibitor lists.
- One company news post (Changshan Fabric, 138th fair) also gave strong evidence.

What didn't:
- English searches that combined product, city and "Canton Fair" mostly returned generic guides.
- Made-in-China showroom pages I checked (Jiangsu James, Changzhou Hengji, Jiangyin Changxu, Hebei Wohua, Hebei Xingye) list no trade shows, so they were dropped.
- I found no Canton Fair evidence for any mill in Changzhou (except the denim mill Kailan), Nantong, Wuxi city, Weifang or Qingdao.
- Shandong mills (Lu Thai, Weiqiao, Huafang) and Jiangsu Sunshine only appear in an undated third-party "known exhibitors" list (jufair.com) or an old 123rd-fair preview, so they are rated medium.

Excluded:
- Changzhou Kingcason (fleece/knit).
- Hebei Textiles Imp. & Exp. (hbtex.com), a trading company that also has home textiles.
- Jiangsu Redsun, Changshu Zhengfangyi and Qiansifang (home textiles).
- Wujiang Mingsike Trading and Suzhou Laiouwei Imp. & Exp. (trading names).
- Shijiazhuang Shuncheng Buye: named at the 137th fair, but I found nothing on its products or factory.

Gaps:
- No booth numbers were found for the 2024-2026 sessions.
- Several company websites (chinakailan.com, boshitex.com, textile-jy.com, jshfcl.com) returned 503 errors.

I never opened cantonfair.org.cn, LinkedIn, Baidu or Global Sources.

What worked best was official government exhibitor lists for recent sessions, published by city and provincial commerce bureaus. These are strong third-party evidence and are not on cantonfair.org.cn. I used: Zhejiang/Shaoxing (136th, 137th), Tai'an (137th), Hubei (137th), Beijing (138th), Jining (136th), Wenzhou Lucheng (138th) and Fuzhou (139th). Company news pages with booth numbers also worked (Loto, Fuyi, Shaoxing Harbour). Generic English searches like "Canton Fair + men's shirts/suits/jeans" mostly returned guides, booth builders and knit or polo makers. Some government PDFs (Quanzhou 138th, the Gansu and Beijing 138th/139th joint-exhibitor lists, Huai'an 137th) were blocked or reset and could not be read. I did not open cantonfair.co, a third-party exhibitor directory, because it may mirror official fair data. Not included because products or woven focus could not be confirmed: Wenzhou Xusheng/Ouyiwei/Yuanda/Sunday (138th Lucheng list), Fujian Jiachen, Fuzhou Haoshijia (139th Fuzhou list), Zhejiang Langshaer Weidi (4 booths, 136th/137th), Feicheng Ouyali, Shandong Jintaida and Tai'an Hongbang (137th Tai'an list). Layer 2 or a later run could research these. Excluded: Zhejiang Welkang (international trading company), Joyord (polo/knit), Fuzhou Xingmao (rainwear), Shaoxing Ruiqin (mainly womenswear) and Shaoxing Huaerjie (listed as wholesaler/trader). No Ningbo shirt factory with Canton Fair evidence was found. The shared web search budget ran out before the Tai'an and Wenzhou names could be researched further, so the list has 12 candidates, not 18.

I found 15 candidates for the womenswear and kids' wear slice, short of the 18 asked for. Only 4 have their own company page or B2B profile behind them. My web searches ran out (the turn limit of 200 searches was reached), so I stopped there. Running more searches would need a follow-up run.

What worked:
- **Company news pages:** Jiaxin Silk (136th and 138th sessions), Honry Kidswear (139th, booth 1.1F01) and Begreat (old sessions only).
- **Official exhibitor lists from local governments:** these gave the most Canton Fair evidence.
  - Guangzhou Commerce Bureau list of companies proposed for 138th general booths (xlsx).
  - Shaoxing lists of 135th and 137th exhibitors (PDF).
  - National table of approved joint exhibitors for the 138th session (PDF, hosted by the Beijing Commerce Bureau). It pairs trading companies with their production partners.

What did not work:
- **Abaya and modest-wear makers:** I found no Canton Fair evidence for any of them. Made-in-China and Alibaba suppliers such as Hangzhou Weimei Garments, AY Collection and Guangzhou Shanel list no trade shows, so I left them out.
- **Product + Canton Fair searches** for Humen, Zhongshan, Changshu, Fujian and Huzhou Zhili mostly returned guides or companies outside scope (outerwear makers in Hebei, military uniforms, lingerie). The Zhili kids' wear group at the 136th session names only brands (优淘, 花田彩, 趣趣么么), with no legal company details.

Gaps for Layer 2:
- Ten of the candidates come only from the official lists. They have no confirmed English name (I give a pinyin transliteration) and no product or woven evidence.
- The 5 joint-exhibition production companies (rated medium) exhibit under a trading company's booth rather than their own.

Excluded:
- Zhejiang Welkang and Veken: trading companies.
- Hebei Loto: outside the slice's regions.
- Wuhan Corhunter/TACEAG: military uniforms, not this slice.
- Sutex Apparel (Nanjing): mixed knit and mostly menswear.
- Changshu Hongyu: leather garments.

I never opened cantonfair.org.cn, and every search call blocked that domain.
